steps.title: Charge
steps.imageAlt: G Pen Micro+ USB-C charging port

bullets.text: Plug a **USB-C cable** into the port on the bottom of the battery.
LED flashes **5 times** when the battery is low.

steps.title: Load
steps.imageAlt: Loading concentrate into the G Pen Micro+

bullets.text: Twist off the **mouthpiece assembly**, then twist off the **tank**.
Add your concentrate to the **ceramic chamber** inside the tank.
Reassemble the tank and mouthpiece before use.

note.text: **Less is more.** A small, rice-sized amount of concentrate works best. Overfilling the chamber clogs the airpath.

steps.title: Set Heat
steps.imageAlt: Setting heat level on the G Pen Micro+

bullets.text: **Click 5 times** to power on. The LED lights up.
**Click 3 times** to cycle through heat levels.

press.sub: 5 clicks to power on or off
Blue = Low · Green = Medium · Red = High

steps.title: Heat & Draw
steps.imageAlt: Heating and drawing from the G Pen Micro+

bullets.text: The LED **flashes then goes solid** when the chamber is ready.
Draw steadily through the mouthpiece while the LED is solid.
Device auto powers off after **5 minutes** of inactivity.

press.sub: Hold button · up to 10 seconds max

note.text: **Hot surface:** Do not touch the tank or tank cover for at least 5 minutes after use.

faq.question: Device won't turn on
faq.answer: Click the button 5 times quickly. If nothing happens, charge the device. The LED will turn red when charging. Make sure the tank is fully twisted onto the battery before trying again.

faq.question: Vapor is thin or weak
faq.answer: Try a higher heat setting. Make sure the concentrate is loaded into the chamber (not on the walls). Clean the tank regularly. Residue buildup on the ceramic reduces efficiency.

faq.question: Airflow feels blocked
faq.answer: Remove the mouthpiece assembly and check for buildup. Soak the mouthpiece in isopropyl alcohol and clean the airpath with a cotton swab. Overfilling the chamber is the most common cause.

faq.question: The LED flashes red and green
faq.answer: Red and green flashing five times means a tank connection problem. Twist off the mouthpiece assembly and the tank, clean the connection threads, then screw the tank back on firmly.
